source.title: Optimal Online Contention Resolution Schemes via Ex-Ante Prophet Inequalities

background: Random-order contention resolution is one of the places where matroid structure gives an unusually clean constant. In a matroid, an ex-ante feasible fractional vector can be rounded online while preserving feasibility as elements arrive. Lee and Singla prove an optimal $1/2$ OCRS for adversarial order and an optimal $(1-1/e)$ random-order contention-resolution scheme for matroids. This constant is tight already for rank one, so the matroid theory is, in that sense, complete. Online resource allocation is broader: a request can consume a vector of resources, may have several feasible assignment options, and the feasible family is not necessarily a matroid even though it is still described by a clean ex-ante relaxation. Will Ma's notes isolate an abstract online resource-allocation model that includes several NRM and stochastic matching formulations. The open problem asks whether the random-order $1-1/e$ phenomenon is really a matroid artifact or a more general consequence of IID/random arrivals plus ex-ante feasibility.
short_statement: Does the optimal $(1-1/e)$ random-order matroid CRS guarantee extend from matroids to the abstract online resource-allocation model used in stochastic allocation and NRM?
full_statement: Let an online resource-allocation instance have a finite horizon $T$, request types arriving either IID from a known distribution or as a uniformly random permutation of a known multiset, and for each realized request type a finite set of feasible actions. Taking an action yields reward and consumes a vector of resources with capacities $B_1,\ldots,B_d$; the online policy observes the request and must choose an action or reject irrevocably while keeping realized resource consumption feasible. Let $\mathrm{FLU}$ be the natural ex-ante/fluid LP that fractionally assigns type-action pairs subject to expected capacity constraints and obtains the corresponding expected reward. In the special case where the feasible accepted sets form a matroid, Lee and Singla's random-order contention-resolution scheme gives the optimal guarantee $1-1/e$ relative to the ex-ante benchmark. The open problem asks whether every instance in the broader abstract online resource-allocation model admits an online policy with expected reward at least $(1-1/e)\mathrm{FLU}$ under IID or random arrival order. If the answer is no, determine the best universal constant and identify the structural property separating matroid-like instances from harder resource-allocation instances.
known_results: Kleinberg and Weinberg introduced matroid prophet inequalities with constant guarantees, and OCRSs were later developed as a general online rounding framework for stochastic selection problems. Lee and Singla designed optimal OCRSs via ex-ante prophet inequalities: an optimal $1/2$ OCRS for adversarial-order matroids and an optimal $(1-1/e)$ random-order contention-resolution scheme for matroids. The $1-1/e$ constant is best possible even for rank one, so the matroid random-order theory is tight. Online stochastic knapsack and multi-unit prophet problems show that LP-relative constants can be characterized for some resource-allocation subcases, but those models do not cover arbitrary type-action systems with multiple resources and non-matroid feasibility. No source checked here proves or refutes the full extension from random-order matroids to Will Ma's abstract resource-allocation model.

where_posed.text: Posed in Will Ma's Online Resource Allocation notes after the discussion of matroid random-order CRS and abstract online resource allocation.
where_posed.location: Remarks around the abstract resource-allocation model

progress.summary: The matroid version is tight at $1-1/e$, and the adversarial-order matroid OCRS is tight at $1/2$. No published result found extends the random-order $1-1/e$ guarantee to the full abstract resource-allocation model.

links.title: Lee and Singla, optimal OCRSs via ex-ante prophet inequalities

counterexample_rationale: A negative answer could plausibly be witnessed by a small resource-allocation instance whose optimal online value is below $(1-1/e)$ times the fluid LP. Such instances are finite and searchable after discretization.
alphaevolve_rationale: Automated search can compare optimal online dynamic programs against the fluid LP for small non-matroid resource-allocation systems and test whether $1-1/e$ is plausible beyond matroids.

literature.synthesis: The strongest existing theorem is matroid-specific. Lee and Singla reduce optimal OCRSs to ex-ante prophet inequalities and obtain the optimal $1/2$ adversarial-order matroid OCRS plus the optimal $(1-1/e)$ random-order CRS. The proof exploits matroid exchange and rank structure. In broader online resource allocation, ex-ante LPs are still central, but feasibility comes from capacities and assignment options rather than a hereditary matroid family. Single-resource stochastic knapsack results show that even one-dimensional capacity can have tight constants below $1-1/e$ in adversarial order; random/IID order may help, but it is unclear whether it restores the matroid constant. The open problem is therefore structural: either find a resource-allocation CRS with the same correlation-gap-style behavior, or construct a non-matroid allocation instance where the fluid LP overstates what random-order online policies can achieve.

reviewed.ref: Euiwoong Lee, Sahil Singla, 'Optimal Online Contention Resolution Schemes via Ex-Ante Prophet Inequalities', ESA 2018
reviewed.result: Designs the first optimal $1/2$ OCRS for matroids and optimal $(1-1/e)$ random-order CRS for matroids.

reviewed.ref: Robert Kleinberg, Seth Matthew Weinberg, 'Matroid Prophet Inequalities', STOC 2012
reviewed.result: Establishes constant prophet inequalities for matroid constraints and supplies the foundational matroid prophet framework.

reviewed.ref: Jiashuo Jiang, Will Ma, Jiawei Zhang, 'Tight Guarantees for Multi-unit Prophet Inequalities and Online Stochastic Knapsack', SODA 2022
reviewed.result: Shows how OCRS formulations capture resource-allocation subproblems and gives tight LP-relative constants for $k$-unit and knapsack settings.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: For a positive result, search for exchange-like properties of the abstract resource-allocation polytope or a randomized rounding that simulates matroid CRS behavior on assignment actions. For a negative result, enumerate small bipartite/action-resource instances, compute the ex-ante LP, and solve the optimal online policy under random order by dynamic programming.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A proof must define the abstract resource-allocation model precisely: request process, known distributions or random-order multiset, action sets, reward/consumption feedback, resource capacities, and stopping rule when a resource is exhausted. The guarantee must be relative to the same ex-ante/fluid LP benchmark used in the statement, not a weaker prophet benchmark or an LP with additional valid inequalities. A positive result must handle general action-resource systems, not only matroids, rank-one constraints, single-resource knapsack, or independently activated elements. A negative result should give a finite instance, compute or certify $\mathrm{FLU}$, and upper-bound the value of every online policy under the stated IID/random-order model. Claims for adversarial order should be labeled separately because the constant can be different.
